text: These are the words of the letter Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the elders, priests, prophets, and all the people Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon
(this was after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the officials, the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the metalworkers had left Jerusalem)
— sent by the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in Babylon. It said:
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Build houses and live in them. Plant gardens and eat what they produce.
Marry and have sons and daughters. Take wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands so they can bear sons and daughters. Multiply there; do not decrease.
Seek the welfare of the city I have sent you to, and pray to the LORD on its behalf, for as it prospers, you too will prosper.
For the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Don't let the prophets and diviners among you deceive you, and don't listen to the dreams you elicit from them.
They are prophesying a lie to you in my name; I have not sent them — this is the LORD's declaration.
For the LORD says this: When Babylon's seventy years are complete, I will attend to you and fulfill my good promise to bring you back to this place.
For I know the plans I have for you — this is the LORD's declaration — plans for your welfare, not for disaster, to give you a future and a hope.
You will call to me and come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.
You will seek me and find me when you search for me with all your heart.

I will be found by you — this is the LORD's declaration — and I will restore your fortunes and gather you from all the nations and places where I banished you, and I will bring you back to the place from which I deported you.
You may say, "The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon" —
but this is what the LORD says about the king who sits on David's throne and about all the people remaining in this city, your countrymen who did not go with you into exile —
this is what the LORD of Armies says: I am about to send sword, famine, and plague against them, and I will make them like rotten figs, too bad to eat.

I will pursue them with sword, famine, and plague, and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a curse and an object of scorn and mockery among all the nations where I have banished them,

because they have not listened to my words — this is the LORD's declaration — words I sent to them again and again through my servants the prophets, though you did not listen — this is the LORD's declaration.
Now hear the word of the LORD, all you exiles I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.

This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying a lie to you in my name: I am about to hand them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will kill them before your eyes.
Because of them a curse will be used by all Judah's exiles in Babylon: "May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire" —

because they have committed an outrage in Israel: they have committed adultery with their neighbors' wives and have spoken a lying word in my name that I did not command them. I know, and I am a witness — this is the LORD's declaration.
Also tell Shemaiah the Nehelamite:
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,
"The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be the officer in the LORD's temple over every madman who acts like a prophet, to put him in the stocks and neck-irons.
So now, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who has been acting like a prophet among you?
For he has sent word to us in Babylon, saying, 'The exile will be long; build houses and live in them, plant gardens and eat what they produce.'"
Zephaniah the priest read this letter aloud to Jeremiah the prophet.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
Send word to all the exiles, saying, "This is what the LORD says about Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you though I did not send him, and has made you trust in a lie —

therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. He will not have anyone living among this people, nor will he see the good I will do for my people — this is the LORD's declaration — because he has preached rebellion against the LORD."
